content.text:
I identified one phase: CsTmO2 (mp-753799).

The simulated CsTmO2 pattern matches the observed peaks closely in both position and relative intensity:

| Observed position (°2θ) | Observed intensity | Simulated intensity |
|---|---|---|
| 12.9 | 12 | 9 |
| 26.15 | 44 | 45 |
| 29.9 | 12 | 9 |
| 31.0 | 22 | 23 |
| 33.75 | 100 | 100 |
| 37.2 | 32 | 31 |
| 40.5 | 14 | 13 |
| 46.0 | 8 | 8 |
| 55.9 | 36 | 35 |
| 58.2 | 27 | 27 |

The weaker peaks between 59° and 79° are also accounted for. As far as I could see, no observed peak is left that would need a second phase.

I only simulated one alternative, YCoO3 (mp-1288734), which some hand-calculated peak positions suggested. Its simulated pattern has a broad, split main peak from about 33.5° to 34.5° and a strong reflection near 47.5°. The observed main peak is single and sharp, and the observed pattern has nothing at 47.5°, so it does not fit. I ruled out the perovskites SrHfO3 and Ba2FeMoO6 by hand, because their strongest peak would sit near 31° rather than 33.75°. The other five candidates were neither calculated nor simulated.

{"present": ["mp-753799"], "confidence": 0.95, "note": "The simulated CsTmO2 pattern reproduces every observed peak position and relative intensity, with no unexplained peaks left over."}
